S23p. 131 — a-series RAZEM vs the column sums

Draft: RAZEM prints 2.386 dymów / 92 / 12.967; the pixel column reads 2387 (incl. raised marks) / 92 exact / 12958.

Why doubtful: The dymy Delta(-1) is the mark-sum law (marks counted). The ludn column is 9 short of the printed 12.967 after every cell was pixel-verified; either one settlement hides a 2-digit value the scan will not yield, or the print's own total is loose.

My reading: keep the printed 12.967 as the truth; the transcription stays as pixel-read.

C. Footnote-marker audit — my work, listed for transparency

Your spot answers exposed the systemic issue: the print sets its footnote markers as inline digits, and OCR fuses them to the neighbouring token ("60⁶ morgów" → "608", "70²" → "70?", "⁴" → "*"). What I changed since your answers: the marker detector now also reads the lines it had skipped and recognises artifact-glyph markers; both OCR models' duplicate detections are removed; markers you identified (pp. 43, 68, 78, 86, 98) are placed at their print-verified anchors, and the false ones (table digits, dates) removed. Label count went 543 → 577 with def-pairing restored on ~40 pages. The audit continues page by page; what remains is below — no action needed from you here.
